cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: A hundred watches. The Company offers a cottage below Lock 7 and a pension in scrip. The gauge on the sill reads what it reads. Somebody else will have to notice.

left.label: Take the cottage
left.outcome: The garden floods every spring. You keep it anyway.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! Magnificent news. Lock 3, Sorrel side. Quieter water, a bigger house, a lower toll book. The Board calls it a promotion and so, Keeper, shall we.

left.label: Accept it
left.outcome: The barge down is the first you have ridden in a year.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Eighty years, a record day, and not one boat grounded. Your name goes on the plaque beside the top gate. Bronze, Keeper. The Meridian spirit, cast in bronze.

left.label: Stand for the unveiling
left.outcome: Bronze goes green, in time. So does everything here.

right.label: Put Quenn's name beside yours
right.outcome: He agrees at once, and means it.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot voted you a chair. Not a title. A chair, by the fire, and a tankard with your name on it. Your Company gave nothing. You knew that.

left.label: Sit in it
left.outcome: "Costs nothing. First thing here that does."

right.label: Give the chair to Dace
right.outcome: Dace sits in it once, to be polite, and never again.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: Your file reads 'reliable'. For the record, that is the Company's highest word. You have kept the gate a hundred watches and never once asked me about the sluice house.

left.label: Ask her now
left.outcome: "No." She almost smiles. "You will find that was the right time."

right.label: Say it was not your business

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: There is a wedding at the Still Water chapel and the whole summit comes, the geese included. The gauge reads what it reads. For once, you are not looking at it.

right.label: Watch the water anyway
right.outcome: Old habits. It is a mark lower than it was.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: It's published. The figures, all of them. The Board has thanked me, blamed the weather, raised the tolls and commissioned a tenth reservoir. Twelve years to fill. Sorry. I thought it would be different.

right.label: The figures were never the whole of it
right.outcome: "No. What was?" You do not know yet.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You have accused me of Dray's death and the Board has accepted it. I am removed. For the record, I did not kill him. For the record, I know where he is. You will not ask.

right.label: Let her go
right.outcome: A new auditor arrives within the week, and asks the same questions.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Done. My principals own the Sorrel half as of this watch. Tolls down, traffic up, and you stay on at a better wage. Delay costs, Keeper, and now it costs me. Shake.

left.label: Shake
left.outcome: Two summers later the pound falls to the sills and nobody in Sorrel knows why.

right.label: Ask what she knows about the water
right.outcome: "That it floats coal. What else is there?"

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Reed Reach is clear. Not a shot, Keeper, not one. The boats went down the west flight this morning. Quieter, isn't it. Our little difficulty, resolved at last.

left.label: It is quieter
left.outcome: Nobody sings at the summit again.

right.label: Ask where they went
right.outcome: "West. Where they came from, one assumes." One assumes wrong.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: Nine nights of the Lamp Vigil, and on the tenth, rain for a week. The pound is full. The chapel is full. We do not ask the water, Keeper. We tend it, and it answers.

left.label: Kneel with the rest
left.outcome: It is a comfort. It is also a wet season.

right.label: Ask how long it will last
right.outcome: "As long as it is tended." She believes it. Almost.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Front page on both shores. THE KEEPER WHO WOULD NOT BEND. You're famous, Keeper. The Company can't dismiss a hero, so it's giving you a lecture tour, and the summit a new Keeper, and the sluice house a new lock.

left.label: Take the tour
left.outcome: You tell the story forty times. It gets shorter.
